scopeReview: IMP-3.A.1: relocation and expansion including contagious, hierarchical and stimulus. Mechanism evidence, retained origin/new adoption, adaptation, migration, overlapping pathways, barriers and scales. No disease model, invented historical route or unsupported unique inference from shape alone.
varietyReview: Contact/adoption map, institutional hierarchy model, adaptation table and relocation ledger. Additional cases distinguish broad/subtype evidence, sequential and cross-scale coexistence, content/contact dimensions, translation barriers, resemblance and goods versus people. All five skills, mixed difficulty and varied keys.
repetitionReview: Mechanism classification is new relative to3.3 effects of cultural patterns. Cases test different dimensions rather than repeated labels: positive evidence versus limits, sequence versus scale, adaptation versus route, count redistribution versus new uptake. No numeric-only clones.
referenceNote: Official topic name and type inventory verified. All examples, diagrams and counts original; no copied classroom activities, external resources or human review claim. Conceptual reasoning is recorded but not independent human certification.

questions.correctOption: Contagious expansion diffusion through neighboring contacts.
questions.independentReview: Checked adoption days0/1/2/3 across ordered neighboring positions15/40/65/90. Mechanism is corroborated by the stated contact-only records, not inferred uniquely from a linear visual pattern.

questions.correctOption: Hierarchical expansion through linked levels of the organization.
questions.independentReview: Followed capital→regional hubs→branch edges and supplied dates, with closer branches explicitly later. Hierarchical means influence/network ordering here, not a universal claim that every large city always adopts first.

questions.correctOption: The underlying idea spreads while ingredients are modified to fit local preferences.
questions.independentReview: Compared constant portable-wrap principle with meat→beans and herb mix→local spice changes. Direct demonstration supplies transmission; adaptation is not inferred merely from superficial similarity.

questions.correctOption: Relocation redistributes 100 practitioners between places without increasing their combined number.
questions.independentReview: Recomputed before100+0=100 and after80+20=100, with origin−20/destination+20. Explicit migration and no other uptake/loss establish the mechanism; equal totals alone would not suffice.

questions.correctOption: Expansion diffusion, while its more specific contact or hierarchy pathway needs more evidence.
questions.independentReview: Separated evidence sufficient for expansion from missing evidence about contact or influence links. No relocation is supplied; choosing a unique subtype would add facts absent from the record.

questions.correctOption: Relocation first, followed by expansion through new adoption.
questions.independentReview: Tracked carrier migration separately from subsequent nonmigrant uptake. Temporal sequencing prevents a false either/or classification of the entire history.

questions.correctOption: The contact pathway can be contagious while the adaptation is also an example of stimulus diffusion.
questions.independentReview: Distinguished mode of contact from transformation of content; both are explicitly provided. The question avoids treating diffusion types as always mutually exclusive dimensions or labeling any change independent invention.

questions.correctOption: A communication barrier can slow diffusion even across a short distance, and translation can change that barrier.
questions.independentReview: Held short distance while varying communication access and noting translation before later adoption. A delay does not prove impossibility; no named language or actual broadcast is represented.

questions.correctOption: Similarity warrants investigation, but does not by itself distinguish diffusion from independent development.
questions.independentReview: Separated resemblance from evidence of historical transmission. The supported conclusion is uncertainty between mechanisms, not proof of either independent invention or a specific diffusion pathway.

questions.correctOption: Objects moving does not establish migration of practitioners; the supplied new learning describes expansion among destination residents.
questions.independentReview: Checked units and mechanism: shipped goods versus practitioners’ residence. Explicit learning plus no craftsperson migration supports expansion, not an assumed relocation merely because an object crossed a border.

questions.correctOption: Hierarchical and contagious pathways can operate at different scales in the same wider spread.
questions.independentReview: Mapped regional organizational links to hierarchical spread and within-town neighboring contacts to contagious expansion. This is spatial-scale coexistence, distinct from the separate earlier relocation-then-expansion sequence.
